title: proactive-telemetry-snapshots-for-oncall
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add opt-in transient telemetry snapshotting to incident-bot: captures a configurable minimal telemetry bundle at responder claim time to accelerate blameless handoffs and root-cause pivots. No default on in hosted customers; admin-configurable in private/dedicated installs.
description:
Motivation: On-call responders frequently spend the first 5-15 minutes gathering context after alert claim (top traces, recent deploys, error logs). This PR introduces a lightweight, time-bounded telemetry snapshot that incident-bot can capture proactively at claim time to reduce cognitive load and improve mean-time-to-resolution.

What this PR does: Adds a transient telemetry capture pipeline that collects a small set of artifacts (top-3 spans by error rate, last 100 log lines for a target service, recent deploy metadata, and metric deltas for key SLOs). Snapshots are stored encrypted for a configurable TTL and are surfaced in the incident thread and the incident-bot UI. Snapshot capture is async and rate-limited to avoid amplifying load during incidents.

Key design points:
- Opt-in by default for hosted (requires admin toggle); enabled-by-default in private installs used in internal QA.
- Snapshot TTL defaults to 1 hour; configurable via incident-bot configmap or admin console.
- Payload is intentionally small (~50-200KB) and sampled to avoid collecting PII.
- Capture runs in a sidecar worker pool with backpressure: at high alert rates, sampling windows widen rather than blocking alert intake.
- All artifacts are labeled with incident metadata and hashed IDs for cross-correlation with observability backends.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated under feature flag "transientTelemetrySnapshots".
- Canary rollout for 10% internal traffic, monitor CPU/IO, snapshot success ratio, and customer-facing latency.
- Gradual increase while monitoring rate-limiter metrics and storage TTL eviction behavior.

Testing done:
- Unit tests for capture orchestration and TTL logic.
- Integration test harness that simulates bursty alerts and validates that sampling/backpressure prevents overrun.
- End-to-end smoke in staging with real observability stubs.

Usage notes:
- Admins can configure what artifact types to include and adjust TTL.
- Responders see a "Snapshot" card in the incident thread with links to the captured artifacts and quick actions (open trace, tail logs).

Related: ENG-4128 implements the UI surface; SUP-2043 documents support workflow for snapshot data access.

Sasha Ivanov: Security review: ensure scrubbers run before snapshot persists. Also we should confirm KMS usage in private installs.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented scrubber pipeline and added KMS config validation in store.go; added docs section about allowed artifact types.
